findings: Unrestricted verification costs only about 2.94% of all visited nodes in this sample; extension/ordering effects account for much of the larger search-tree difference.
2% quota admits fewer proofs and reduces aggregate main nodes by about15.81%, but changes two root moves including the endgame; tactical quality is unknown.
5% quota slightly increases the main tree despite four skipped proofs, demonstrating nonlinear feedback rather than monotonic efficiency.
10% quota is nonbinding in this pilot and reproduces unrestricted moves, scores and node counts.
No quota is selected or promoted from this four-position pilot.
limitations: Concurrent frozen confirmation load; one timing sample per mode, no timing significance claim
Different search trees/moves invalidate identical-work speed attribution
Node share is not wall-time share; admitted proof can overshoot target
Four positions cannot establish tactical robustness or Elo

decision.next: Tactical/endgame holdouts and paired equal-time study; RIFT real signal collection separately
